transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01 15:00 PT | Duration: 58m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (SE), Priya Rao (CSM) - Redwood; Jared Kim (Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Platform), Eliot Cho (Security), Mina Park (PM) - AurumX

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros then we ll jump into the onboarding runbook and what the first two weeks look like. Uh, quick note, recording is on.
[00:18] Jared: Cool, thanks Maya. We re excited to get this moving; we have a tight Q3 goal to ship inference for our customer support assistant. Main blockers are network + compliance.
[00:33] Priya: Great, high level agenda: run through the onboarding steps, VPC/network intake, security checklist, sample workload and pilot definition, then next steps.
[00:47] Liam: I'll cover the infra bits — how staging works, typical batching and KV cache patterns, and what we need from you for a smooth pilot.
[01:05] Sofia: On the platform side we use k8s with an internal ingress and egress rules; we re prefer private connectivity. We d like to understand Redwood Private options and if we need an on prem box.
[01:24] Maya: For private, we have a few patterns — VPC peering, private link, and on-prem package. Most customers start with VPC peering to our private control plane; if you need full air-gap we can talk about the on-prem bundle. For your use-case, VPC peering sounds right.
[01:45] Eliot: From security, can you share SOC 2 Type II artifacts, SAML SSO support, and encryption key management? Also curious about audit logs retention and redaction capabilities.
[02:03] Priya: Absolutely, we will share SOC2 certificate and our security pack. We can provide sample audit log output; note that logs sometimes have obfuscated ids — we ll show format. SAML and SSO are supported. KMS integration for customer keys is available for Private deployments.
[02:26] Jared: For perf, our latency budget is 200ms p95 for single-turn queries. Is that realistic on hosted or do we need Dedicated GPUs?
[02:40] Liam: 200ms p95 is tight depending on model size. For smaller quantized models and good batching we can be sub-200ms on Dedicated capacity. Hosted can hit that for some smaller models and with prefix caching but it's less predictable during bursts. There's tradeoff between cost and latency.
[03:02] Mina: Can you say more about caching? We re concerned about cold-starts.
[03:10] Liam: Sure — we have prefix/KV caching and continuous batching. If your workload has repeat prompts (like templated support replies), cache helps a lot. Also we can tune batch windows to balance latency/cost per token.
[03:27] Jared: We'll send a token distribution and sample conversations so you can suggest batching and quantization configs.
[03:33] Maya: Perfect.
[03:36] [04:00] — brief cross talk about calendars —
[04:15] Eliot: On compliance — do you support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS)? We need all PII encrypted with our keys while at rest.
[04:27] Priya: Yes for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and can work on dedicated keys for enterprise plans.
[04:41] Sofia: Network wise: what do you need for route tables and egress? We have restricted internet egress.
[04:51] Liam: We'll need a few IP ranges for the staging endpoints and ephemeral ports for model updates. If you re doing strict egress, VPC peering eliminates most egress needs; we'll share a minimal whitelist.
[05:06] Jared: Pilot scope — we re thinking two-week PoC with 10k daily requests, ramp to 50k by end of quarter. Success is meet 200ms p95 and maintain <=0.5% error rate.
[05:22] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose a pilot plan: week 1 instrument + baseline tests in staging; week 2 run ramp and ops handoff. We'll provide dashboards and cost projections.
[05:35] Mina: Who will be the primary contacts during the pilot?
[05:39] Maya: Priya will be your CSM, Liam handles infra/benchmarks, and I ll coordinate commercial and rollout.
[05:48] [06:00] — 6 minutes in —
[06:05] Liam: On metrics, we ll instrument token-level cost, p50/p95 latencies, and per-route error breakdown. We can also attach traces to specific requests if you provide sample ids.
[06:20] Sofia: For staging access, how do we authenticate? SSO or API keys?
[06:26] Priya: We can support SAML SSO for team access; for programmatic onboarding we'll issue scoped API keys and can lock them to an IP range.
[06:37] Jared: Any gotchas with data residency? We need EU-only data residency for a subset of customers.
[06:44] Maya: We have region pinning; we can route EU traffic to EU-hosted clusters and keep data in-region. For Private, that's configurable.
[06:55] Eliot: Can we get an example of your rollback/fallback policy if a model deploy causes quality regression?
[07:03] Liam: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variant. Also Redwood Optimize can monitor evals and trigger alerts on regressions against a prompt set.
[07:15] Mina: What's the typical time to onboard to staging?
[07:19] Priya: For simple VPC peering and a small pilot, 3-5 business days once we have the network info and a point of contact. On-prem takes longer.
[07:30] Jared: We're leaning VPC peering. I'll have networking send the route table and firewall rules.
[07:36] Maya: Great. We'll send a checklist today.
[07:39] [08:02] — discussion of pricing high-level —
[08:12] Maya: For pilot we'll give a temporary eval credit; once we move to Dedicated we ll provide commit options and a cost/latency tradeoff matrix.
[08:25] Jared: Competitor question — we did an internal eval vs VendorX and our own stack; curious how Redwood handles multitenant isolation.
[08:34] Liam: Dedicated pools with tenant isolation and per-tenant quotas are standard; for extra isolation we do single-tenant Dedicated clusters.
[08:43] Eliot: About logs — need them in our SIEM; can you push audit logs or do we need to pull?
[08:50] Priya: We can push to your SIEM or provide S3 delivery. The logs are in standard JSON; sometimes product names are abbreviated in auto transcriptions — but the fields are stable.
[08:59] Mina: Is there a recommended eval set or tooling?
[09:03] Maya: We'll share our eval harness and a sample prompt set; Redwood Optimize can run periodic checks and surface regressions.
[09:12] Jared: Okay next steps — we ll send token profile and sample prompts; please send runbook and staging access. Also want the SOC2 and SAML schema.
[09:23] Maya: Confirmed. We'll attach a short SLO template for pilot and a suggested monitoring dashboard.
[09:31] Eliot: One more thing — vulnerability scanning, do you allow us to scan the staging endpoints?
[09:37] Priya: Yes, we allow authenticated scanning in staging; we'll coordinate scope.
[09:43] [10:00] — closing recap by Maya —
[10:05] Maya: Quick recap: 1) Redwood sends onboarding runbook, SOC2 pack, example logs, and SSO integration notes; 2) AurumX shares workload tokens, prompts, and network rules; 3) schedule infra deep dive with Liam; 4) set pilot dates and SLOs. Action owners in the notes. Any final Qs?
[10:26] Jared: Nope, all clear. Thanks team.
[10:29] Maya: Thanks everyone, we ll follow up with the packet.
[10:33] Meeting ends.
